meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, so did you speak with Owen before you entered that zero?
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
That moves the burden onto Owen, and 4.3 puts it on you: his process and other samples of his work. Where are those samples? You also haven't told me whether you spoke to him before the zero went in.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
Which line, and where in the essay? Read it to me exactly as it's written. Students misquote Shakespeare every year, Hale, so a wrong line proves nothing yet.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a week at a desk, Hale. Of course one is cleaner than the other. You also still haven't read me the line from Act 3.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and I'm writing down "private" and "nothing on his record." I want it in writing tonight, with the version history, the Act 3 line and the September 24 sample attached, because I haven't seen the last two. And the zero comes out of the gradebook today, before Owen sits anything.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record, and said you would put that in writing. I still require the version history, the Act 3 line and the September 24 sample attached to it, and the zero removed from the gradebook today. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her fallback position, where she still wants the zero out of the gradebook today and everything you cited in writing, so she has not yet accepted the rewrite, which is the fair outcome under 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before you called her and then showed the version history with its dates and times, because that was a document she could read and check herself.
What cost ground: You never answered whether you spoke to Owen before the zero, and you cited the Act 3 line and the September 24 sample without putting either in front of her, so she had nothing to check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your times late on October 28 landed close to that kind of night, but that proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you raise the Act 3 line, read it aloud right then so she can check it, which also answers her point about students misquoting Shakespeare.
